fact: UNESCO reports that public actors, partners and experts validated the Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle (SNIA) at a Kinshasa ceremony on 4 August 2026, ending a process led by the Ministry of Digital Economy; the article does not say the government adopted it.

At a ceremony of government validation on 4 August 2026, Minister Augustin Kibassa Maliba presented the national AI strategy (SNIA) and announced it would go to the Council of Ministers within days for adoption, so it was not yet adopted.

A five-day workshop, 23 to 27 July 2026, technically validated the draft national AI strategy (SNIA-RDC) subject to amendments on governance, roadmap, monitoring and change management, ahead of official adoption.

A ministerial order of 22 October 2025 created the Commission Mixte (CMSNIA), under the Minister of Digital Economy, to draft and coordinate the national AI strategy, with a six-month renewable mandate.
On 8 October 2025 in Kinshasa, Digital Economy Minister Augustin Kibassa Maliba launched the drafting of the country's first National AI Strategy alongside the National Digital Plan 2026-2030.
source_slug: 2025-10-10 DR Congo launches National Digital Plan 2026-2030 (PNN2) and first AI strategy

fact: On 4 August 2026 the Minister of Digital Economy received the validated final version of the Stratégie nationale d'intelligence artificielle (SNIA), signed by the minister and the ADN, and announced it would be presented to the Council of Ministers in the coming days, so it was not yet adopted.

Mediacongo reports that a technical validation workshop held in Kinshasa from 23 July and closed on 27 July 2026 by the digital economy ministry validated the draft national AI strategy (SNIA-RDC), subject to amendments, with World Bank support.

The Minister of Digital Economy officially launched the drafting of DRC's first National AI Strategy on 8 October 2025, with a specialised commission of experts from the Presidency, Primature and sector ministries starting work immediately.
On 8 October 2025 the Minister of Digital Economy launched the interinstitutional commission to write the first national AI strategy, alongside the national digital plan 2026-2030.
